newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister sees striking doctors, won't yield.
newsitem.headline: French minister sees striking doctors, won't yield.

text.p: French Social Affairs Minister Jacques Barrot met junior hospital doctors on the 16th day of their strike on Friday but vowed the government would go ahead with a disputed health cost control plan.

Barrot and junior minister Herve Gaymard met a delegation of strikers at the health ministry after hospital doctors from across France staged a show of force in Paris on Thursday, with at least 10,000 people taking part in a protest march.
The doctors, on strike in 22 of the country's 26 teaching hospitals, are demanding the scrapping of automatic fines on doctors in regions which exceed government health spending targets.
But Barrot told Europe 1 radio the measure was essential as a safeguard against overspending until new standard medical procedures took root.
The centre-right government has imposed health spending curbs to bring down the welfare deficit and help France qualify for a single European currency in 1999.
Barrot said the government would probably formally promulgate an agreement between the national health insurance fund and two health professionals' trade unions which support the reform on Saturday.
